items.title: Michael Moore interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: I feel the same way. Like T.S. Monk’s band, you know Thelonious Monk Junior, I mean I heard them and they have arrangements and they’re not reading music, they have their act together.

ctx.x: Did you two end up playing together?

We did, yeah, which also had its flip side to it. My father was also very particular about the bass notes. And he would take me on jobs when I was about fifteen years old, and when I was just finding my way around on the instrument, and I had to go out and fake 30 or 40 tunes in an hour. And as you might expect, I played a lot of wrong notes, and he was not very understanding about it. He somehow thought that I should just know them by a kind of magic. And so that’s why I’m still in therapy, Monk, after all these…
Well gee, faking tunes you don’t know on the bass, I mean that’s about as hard as you could get.
